doc: Area-weighted 10-bin histogram of the 256x128 Earth reference. np.histogram bins [edge_k, edge_k+1), the last bin closed, edges = linspace(0, 1, bins + 1) computed in float64 (k * (1 / bins)) and rounded to the IMAGE dtype (float32 edges for a float32 image); values outside [0, 1] are dropped; weights cos(lat) in float64, normalized by their sum. Byte-derived maps put thousands of texels exactly on the edges 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 (51k / 255): a port must send a texel equal to a float32 edge to the UPPER bin (a one-ulp change of the input moves the L1 mass by 0.03 to 0.09). With that tie rule the result is a float64 sum of weights: 1e-9. Input convention: the u8 input(s) img are maps stored as bytes, and the function receives them as float32(u8) / float32(255) (`u8.astype(np.float32) / 255.0`: the division is done, and correctly rounded, in float32, as measure.load reads an 8-bit map), NOT as the raw bytes and NOT as a float64 quotient (a texel on a histogram edge or a threshold would move). params.u8_inputs lists them.

u8_inputs.img: float32(u8) / float32(255), the division in float32
